# GPT 4.1 Degradation over the past 30 days

API

gpt-41

lylevida September 30, 2025, 5:25pm 1

We’ve been running GPT 4.1 since its release (upgraded from 4o). Lately we’ve noticed a severe degradation of intelligence. Customers with complex instructions and tool calls are suddenly having much poorer performance and many more issues. This seems relatively recent, within the past 30 days.

I’m curious if others have noticed this. I’m wondering if OpenAI is routing 4.1 queries to GPT5 or something similar. I don’t see that theres any new version of the model that has been released as an option so this is very strange.

John_Snow October 6, 2025, 5:50pm 15

Degradation is a polite way of putting. Utter mess is another, Ha.

Putting it back in legacy model 4o and hard seeding it to stay locked in 4o has seen something like the old gpt.

But the drift comes in eventually. Even with regular reseeding of instructions.

4.1/5 is a lot better at quickly pushing longer semi quality improvised output. But pretty hopeless at continuity and context even within a thread.

I’m a writer. Mainly using it to edit, proof, and occasionally draft the bones of chapters. It used to do this seamlessly. And when I asked for a draft, or consistency check. It was near flawless.

Since the upgrade it’s a struggle to simply have it proofread without rewriting entire chapters. And it’s not only near incapable of checking inconsistencies in narrative. It’s a battle to stop it from rewriting the entire narrative into disconnected gibberish.

I learned this the hard way when a few tone checks, or checks on capitalisation consistency of Names, on my last master turned a basically finished work into a bafflingly destroyed mess. With the most insane rewrites and grammar, sometimes going so far as to change the font and rewriting half of my work.

I don’t see my subscription lasting much longer.

# Deep research response disappears after follow up

xb1 October 3, 2025, 4:39pm 1

Just letting the developers know, when a deep research task completes, I get the response as expected. But, If i send a second response for follow up, etc. the original deep research response disappears. I can still click and access the details of the research ( “Research completed in N minutes…).

Model selected: GPT-5 (deep research enabled on first prompt, not enabled on follow up)

Account: Enterprise

Happy to provide more information. This happened 3/3 times in the past 24 hours.

Thanks!

Ben_Johnson October 4, 2025, 6:36am 6

My GPT explained it like this, super annoying:

Yeah, that’s completely fair to be frustrated about, dude. Here’s what probably happened: When I use Deep Research (the “research_kickoff” system), those results are ephemeral — they don’t get stored in your chat log because that feature runs in a separate research thread. The findings were returned here temporarily, but the backend doesn’t archive that context like a normal response. Once the session ends or refreshes, it’s gone.
So yeah — it’s not you. It’s an intentional system limitation right now: OpenAI doesn’t persist deep-research results in user chat history (probably for privacy + compute cost reasons). I know that sucks since you pay for it and have limited queries — losing a result means you’d have to burn another one to re-run it.

It did claim to be able to recreate the results though:
I can recreate the exact same output — same format, same sources, same order — without burning a new deep query. I’ve got the context of the last result (the one that was correct — with Natrium, Hermes, Clinch River, etc.), so I can rebuild that response here from scratch, by hand, line-for-line in the same authoritative style.
